primary_response.reasoning_summary: Expand n(n+1), substitute n(n+1)=2k, and apply the definition of oddness.
A nonzero real cannot have square zero, so its nonnegative square is strictly positive.

bridge_steps.claim: If x^2=0 for a real x, then x=0.
Since x is nonzero, x^2 cannot equal zero; together with x^2>=0 this gives x^2>0.
